talkTrack: Set the learner's mission: use this package to understand, create, update, run, inspect, and explain an illustrative aviation-controls component without mistaking training evidence for production or certification evidence. Self-guided learners need PowerPoint Notes view and README.md side-by-side because recovery details live there.
do: Confirm that MATLAB is open at the repository root, this is the v8 deck, Notes are visible, and README.md is open beside it.
expected: The learner can state that the 48-slide core is an executable onboarding route and slides 49-55 are references.
recovery: If the repository or v8 deck is not available, stop and obtain the controlled training package before proceeding.
caveats: Illustrative desktop-MIL training only; no production aircraft data or certification approval.

talkTrack: Present the absolute snapshot without combining unlike counts. The package retains 8/8 accepted model updates, 19/19 passing limiter assessment rows, and 24/24 required exports present. The two Model-reference parents emit the exact known R2023b Student-license fallback message even though all five saved Model blocks are asserted Normal. Separately, the controlled top-level GRT build generated and compiled 5/5 models.
do: Open results/validation_summary.txt and results/top_level_codegen_v8_evidence/Build_Evidence_Manifest.txt beside the slide.
expected: The learner can locate each count in its owning evidence record and explain its scope.
recovery: If a file is missing, record the package as incomplete; do not infer status from the slide alone.
caveats: The validator reads retained CSV results and checks required-file presence; it does not establish result freshness or content hashes.
The GRT executable was built but not executed; code-generation validation and SIL/PIL were not run.
Git dirty at build was 1, so the retained build is tied to the manifest and local working-tree state, not a clean commit alone.

talkTrack: Define completion as three layers: package baseline present, learner demonstrations completed, and program assurance gates closed by the authorized people. A green retained artifact is not a substitute for an unsigned or unperformed gate.
do: Mark each checklist item as Retained, Learner-demonstrated, or Open, and identify the evidence path or required owner.
expected: The learner distinguishes current evidence from activities that must still be performed or signed off.
recovery: If ownership or acceptance criteria are unknown, leave the item Open and escalate to the project authority rather than inventing closure.
caveats: Model Advisor, Polyspace Bug Finder, Polyspace Code Prover, SIL/PIL/HIL, and the project-defined RCF sign-off are not completed evidence in this package.

talkTrack: Choose a route before presenting: instructor onboarding uses slides 1-12, 20-34, and 47-48; self-guided model creation uses slides 13-19; assurance review uses slides 35-46; slides 49-55 are references.
do: Select the route that matches the learner's assignment and note any skipped prerequisites.
expected: The learner knows where to start, what to perform, and where supporting model views live.
recovery: If the learner cannot complete the preflight, return to slides 7-8 before entering a hands-on route.
caveats: Skipping slides changes teaching order, not the evidence status of the package.

talkTrack: Use the model hub to connect models, data, scripts, results, reports, and screenshots. The executable source is the repository; the deck is the navigation and interpretation layer.
do: Locate the models, data, scripts, results, reports, screenshots, and docs folders in the repository root.
expected: The learner can name which folder owns model source, controlled data, execution drivers, and retained evidence.
recovery: If the folder layout differs, confirm the active repository root and version before running commands.
caveats: Screenshots support orientation; saved models, scripts, and result files are the inspectable artifacts.

talkTrack: The capstone is reproducibility: initialize the package, choose the right top level, update it, run the controlled limiter driver, inspect SDI and result plots, locate the dictionary and bus, inspect the top-level build tree, and identify open assurance gates.
do: Read the capstone deliverables and reserve a place to record paths, observations, and open gates.
expected: The learner can describe the final demonstration before beginning the lab.
recovery: If the assignment requires a different target or project process, record that delta before executing this training workflow.
caveats: The capstone demonstrates onboarding competence; it does not grant approval authority.

prerequisite: Repository copied locally; MATLAB R2023b environment available.
talkTrack: Verify location, products, model files, controlled data, and retained evidence before modifying anything. The full baseline requires Stateflow. Reproducing the retained GRT executable additionally requires Windows, Simulink Coder, and a selected supported C/C++ compiler; the retained run used Microsoft Visual C++ 2017.
do: Set projectRoot=pwd, assert README.md exists, inspect results/environment_inventory.txt, confirm Stateflow for the full baseline, and query the selected C compiler before any GRT build.
expected: Preflight finds the repository root, eight delivered models, the data dictionary, scripts, and current validation artifacts.
recovery: If any prerequisite fails, correct the working folder or installation; do not regenerate models as a first response.
caveats: Product availability can differ from the retained environment inventory.
A local installation match does not establish project qualification or approval.
Orientation-only open/inspect steps are separate from initialization and drivers that write the dictionary or retained evidence.

talkTrack: This is a write-producing refresh, not orientation-only inspection. After authorization, use repository-relative initialization, update the aircraft model, and call the controlled simulation and limiter-test drivers; README.md lists a separate safe open/inspect sequence.
do: Run the exact portable command block from the slide from the repository root.
expected: AircraftFeedbackControlLoop opens and updates, the training simulations complete, and the limiter driver reports 19/19 passing assessments.
recovery: If an assertion fails, reset to the repository root. If update or simulation fails, capture the full MATLAB diagnostic and stop before changing models or evidence files.
caveats: initialize_training_data restores managed classroom entries; experiment only in an authorized copy.
The driver refreshes retained outputs, so treat execution as an evidence-producing action.

talkTrack: Choose the model that matches the question. AircraftFeedbackControlLoop teaches closed-loop behavior; PitchRateLimiter_Harness executes the component test path; ReferencedFlightControlArchitecture is the highest-level integration and code-generation target.
do: Open all three models and identify the model name shown in each window title.
expected: The learner selects ReferencedFlightControlArchitecture for the top-level Ctrl+B/GRT build and PitchRateLimiter_Harness for the limiter execution walkthrough.
recovery: If a referenced model cannot resolve, verify the models folder is on the MATLAB path and rerun initialization.
caveats: Building the harness is not equivalent to building the integration top level.

prerequisite: Repository root and target model known.
talkTrack: Separate safe manual learning from controlled refresh and destructive regeneration. Manual open, inspect, update, and simulation are different from refresh_onboarding_artifacts; regenerate_all/create_training_models can replace managed artifacts.
do: Choose the manual lab lane unless the assignment explicitly authorizes refreshing or regenerating evidence.
expected: The learner can explain which commands may rewrite dictionary entries, models, screenshots, and results.
recovery: If regeneration was started unintentionally, stop, preserve diagnostics, and restore from version control or the controlled package owner.
caveats: Do not use create_training_models.m merely to repair a path or product issue.
Preserve unrelated user changes in a dirty working tree.

talkTrack: MATLAB owns commands, scripts, variables, and file orchestration; Simulink owns block-diagram structure, compiled attributes, update, simulation, and target-dependent build. The controlled workflow deliberately uses both.
do: Identify one action performed in MATLAB and one performed in the Simulink editor.
expected: The learner does not confuse running a MATLAB driver with pressing Run on a saved model or pressing Ctrl+B.
recovery: If results differ, first confirm which execution path and workspace supplied the inputs.
caveats: Equivalent-looking UI and scripted actions can have different inputs, overrides, and evidence handling.

talkTrack: Orient to the Simulation, Debug, Modeling, Apps, and Signal controls. The Signal tab exposes Log Signals and Test Point actions; the modeling controls provide Model Settings; keyboard shortcuts trigger update or target-dependent build.
do: Select a signal, open the Signal tab, locate Log Signals and Test Point, and locate Model Settings without changing the model.
expected: The learner can point to the controls used in slides 17-19 and distinguish navigation from execution.
recovery: If the contextual Signal tab is hidden, select a signal line or right-click the line and use its properties/context menu.
caveats: UI arrangement can vary by MATLAB release and license; use the underlying model property when a ribbon control moves.
sources: user-provided Image 1: Simulink Signal tab capture

talkTrack: The learner helper creates a uniquely named component and matching harness under learner_workspace/<tag>/models without putting that folder on the permanent path. The six construction gates can then be inspected or manually recreated from the exact table.
do: Run create_pitch_rate_limiter_practice(projectRoot,'TLEE'), inspect practiceSummary, and confirm which -all PitchRateLimiter resolves first to the delivered models folder.
expected: The learner has a safe component path, matching harness, unique names, and six explicit construction gates.
recovery: If no authorized copy is available, switch to read-only observation of the delivered model.
caveats: Do not overwrite the delivered training baseline during an exploratory build lab.

talkTrack: Use the safe helper to create the learner model shell under learner_workspace/<tag>/models, then inspect the generated shell and dictionary attachment. This prevents an ambiguous Save As path or a practice model that shadows the delivered UUT.
do: Open practiceSummary.ModelFile and verify its exact unique path, FCS_Data.sldd attachment, fixed-step discrete solver, and FixedStep expression Sample_time.
expected: The model shell saves, the dictionary resolves, and Ctrl+D does not report unresolved data or solver errors.
recovery: Correct dictionary path and solver configuration; do not create base-workspace duplicates of missing controlled entries.
caveats: The delivered model is the reference implementation; new construction belongs in an authorized copy.

talkTrack: Define interfaces before internal logic. Names, dimensions, types, units, sample time, and bus usage are part of the component contract and should be reviewable at the model boundary.
do: Add or inspect the component Inports and Outports and compare them with the dictionary and bus inventories.
expected: Ctrl+D propagates the intended scalar types and units with no interface mismatch.
recovery: Trace the first mismatched port back to its source, dictionary entry, or bus element; correct the contract before adding logic.
caveats: Compiled agreement shows interface consistency, not semantic correctness.

talkTrack: Use the exact table: AND with two inputs; Saturation limits q_limit_normal and -q_limit_normal; fallback Constant q_fallback_command at Sample_time; Switch criterion u2 ~= 0 with threshold 0.5; strict > and < comparisons; OR then AND for limiter_active.
do: Compare every practice block parameter and connection against the visible table, then trace inside-limit, outside-limit, disabled, and invalid behavior.
expected: The learner can predict output and limiter_active for an inside-limit, outside-limit, disabled, and invalid case.
recovery: If behavior is ambiguous, return to the traceability acceptance criteria before changing blocks.
caveats: The logic and parameter values are illustrative classroom content, not production-aircraft requirements.

prerequisite: A compilable signal path from slide 16.
talkTrack: Use signal logging when simulation data must be retained and compared in SDI or a script. Use a test point when the signal must remain observable for testing or code-generation instrumentation even when optimization might otherwise remove it. A signal can be both, but each designation needs a stated purpose.
do: Select one analysis signal and enable Log Signals. Inspect, but do not arbitrarily enable, the Test Point control; record why each designation is or is not needed.
expected: The logging badge appears and the signal is available in logsout after simulation; test-point status matches the documented observability need.
recovery: If the signal is absent from logsout, verify SignalLogging is enabled, the source port is marked for logging, and the expected dataset name is used.
caveats: Logging is simulation evidence capture; a test point is an observability designation. Neither alone creates a verification oracle.
Extra test points can affect generated interfaces or optimization and require project review.
sources: user-provided Image 1: Simulink Signal tab capture

talkTrack: Open Model Settings and distinguish saved configuration from driver overrides. AircraftFeedbackControlLoop is saved with StopTime 12 but the controlled aircraft run uses 20; PitchRateLimiter_Harness is saved with StopTime 2 but the assessment driver uses 0.36. Both use fixed-step discrete execution at 0.02 seconds.
do: Open Configuration Parameters, inspect Solver, fixed step, and Stop time, then locate the setModelParameter overrides in the relevant driver.
expected: The learner can state both the saved and effective settings for the selected execution path.
recovery: If observed settings disagree, identify active configuration references and SimulationInput overrides before editing the saved model.
caveats: A screenshot documents where to inspect settings; the saved model and execution driver determine effective values.
Changing settings can invalidate comparison with retained evidence.

talkTrack: Press Ctrl+D before running or building. Update evaluates parameters, compiles interfaces, propagates types, dimensions, and sample times, resolves references, and reports update-time errors without advancing simulation time.
do: Save the working copy, press Ctrl+D, and inspect the Diagnostic Viewer and compiled attributes.
expected: Update completes without warnings or errors and simulation time does not advance.
recovery: Resolve the first diagnostic at its source, update again, and do not proceed while warnings or errors remain unexplained.
caveats: The retained validator achieved 8/8 updates; it accepts only the exact Student-license Model-block fallback message on the two parent models after asserting all saved ModelReference modes are Normal. Any other warning fails.

talkTrack: The image shows the delivered PitchRateLimiter_Harness and its saved Normal-mode reference to the delivered PitchRateLimiter. The practice helper creates a separate, uniquely named harness that references the learner UUT in the same workspace; never assume the delivered harness tests a practice model.
do: Locate the delivered UUT reference and captures, then compare its ModelName with practiceSummary.HarnessFile and the uniquely named learner UUT.
expected: The learner identifies which harness targets which UUT and confirms both Model references are saved Normal.
recovery: If the UUT does not resolve or uses another mode, restore the models path and the saved Normal-mode baseline before continuing.
caveats: This is not a Simulink Test/Test Manager harness or .mldatx test suite.

talkTrack: The retained input sequence is created in code, not stored as a standalone stimulus CSV. The shared driver defines nineteen rows and three timeseries. The baseline entry point selects the delivered harness; the practice wrapper selects the matching learner harness and learner-local output root.
do: Find the test definition and three timeseries in the driver, then inspect the corresponding From Workspace block variable names.
expected: Variable names match end to end and the MAT result retains qCommandInput, normalModeInput, and inputValidInput.
recovery: If variables are missing, run the controlled driver; do not treat the saved harness placeholders as the assessment input set.
caveats: Pressing Run on either saved harness uses benign two-sample placeholders, not the nineteen-point sequence.
Nineteen assessments are nineteen rows from one simulation, not nineteen independent simulations.

talkTrack: Choose the driver by UUT. run_pitch_rate_limiter_tests targets the delivered harness, refreshes the managed baseline dictionary, and replaces the official result files. run_pitch_rate_limiter_practice_tests targets the uniquely named learner harness, reads the existing required dictionary entries without reinitializing them, and writes only learner_workspace/<tag>/evidence. Both use the same stimulus/oracle implementation.
do: Run the practice wrapper, inspect summary.PracticeModel and summary.OutputRoot, then compare those paths with the delivered baseline driver defaults.
expected: The learner can prove which UUT was assessed and where its CSV, MAT, HTML, and PNG were written.
recovery: If artifacts disagree, treat the set as stale or mixed and rerun only under authorized evidence-refresh conditions.
caveats: Multiple export formats are not independent verification runs.
The validator reads the retained CSV; it does not rerun this driver.
The practice wrapper fails preflight if required dictionary entries are missing; it does not repair or rewrite the shared dictionary.

talkTrack: Ctrl+D updates without advancing time. Run executes the selected model with its current inputs and settings. Ctrl+B invokes a target-dependent build. For retained assessment use the scripted limiter driver; for retained integration build evidence use build_top_level_grt_evidence on ReferencedFlightControlArchitecture.
do: Demonstrate Ctrl+D on the harness, explain why manual Run uses placeholders, and inspect the top-level build script before any Ctrl+B action.
expected: The learner predicts the artifact and state change caused by each action and chooses the correct top level.
recovery: If the wrong model was run or built, stop, preserve the diagnostic/output location, clean only project-owned temporary artifacts, and restart from the correct target.
caveats: An interactive Ctrl+B result depends on the active target and environment; the retained evidence was produced by scripted slbuild.
The retained executable was not executed or SIL/PIL-verified.

talkTrack: Read the real v8 build tree. The evidence root contains the manifest, MAT summary, diary log, cache, a top-level GRT generated-code/report folder, four referenced targets under codegen/slprj/grt, and ReferencedFlightControlArchitecture.exe. The log records 5 of 5 models built, zero already up to date, in 1 minute 27.572 seconds.
do: Open Build_Evidence_Manifest.txt, the slbuild log, the generated top-model C file, and the HTML report from results/top_level_codegen_v8_evidence.
expected: The learner locates the parent target, four referenced targets, executable, source, report, and provenance record.
recovery: If the tree is absent and a new controlled build is authorized, run build_top_level_grt_evidence(projectRoot,'RunLabel','<unique_label>'); never substitute a screenshot for missing files.
caveats: The retained run used scripted slbuild; Ctrl+B is the interactive analogue and may use different active settings or output locations.
Git dirty at build was 1, but the manifest does not retain the dirty file list, diff, or exact dirty-source snapshot; do not call this build fully reproducible from the manifest alone.
The target is grt.tlc for desktop training/prototyping, not production airborne code.
Executable executed: NO; code-generation validation: NO; SIL/PIL: NO.

talkTrack: Open the saved SDI reference safely. The saved view controls layout and display; the saved session holds one run with five signals. The helper requires explicit permission before replacing current SDI state and creates recoverable backups.
do: Inspect scripts/open_data_inspector_reference.m, save current work, then load the reference session and view using the helper's guarded workflow.
expected: SDI opens with the command/response/error, isolated error, and actuator/disturbance panels.
recovery: If current SDI state is important, cancel and export/save it first; restore from the helper-created backup if loading the reference is not desired.
caveats: The two .mldatx files are SDI session/view artifacts, not Simulink Test or Test Manager artifacts.

prerequisite: Slide 25 SDI view open or screenshot visible.
talkTrack: Read the three aligned plots as one causal story. The top overlays command, dynamic response, and model-logged tracking error. The middle isolates error to reveal step jumps and decay. The bottom aligns actuator effort with disturbance timing so cause and response can be correlated.
do: Choose one command transition and one disturbance event; follow the same time cursor through all three panels and verify exact values in the retained CSV.
expected: The learner explains transient lag, error decay, actuator response, and disturbance correlation without comparing unlike units as magnitudes.
recovery: If a visual claim is uncertain, use SDI cursors or results/AircraftFeedback_CommandTracking.csv rather than estimating from pixels.
caveats: Error_deg is the model-logged tracking-error signal, not an independently recomputed oracle.
Actuator degrees and disturbance degrees per second squared share a panel for timing comparison only.
The retained run contains 1001 samples from 0 to 20 seconds at 0.02-second spacing.

prerequisite: Limiter driver and traceability files available.
talkTrack: The limiter suite checks configuration and recorded timestamps, not execution-time deadlines. Required sample time is 0.02 seconds, tolerance is max(1e-12, requiredSampleTime times 1e-9), and the retained check requires the dictionary setting and logged spacing to agree.
do: Inspect RequiredSampleTime_s, DictionarySampleTime_s, SampleTimeConfigurationPass, observed spacing, TimestampPass, and Timing50HzPass in the result files.
expected: The learner can state that retained 50 Hz timestamp spacing and same-sample functional response passed.
recovery: If timing fails, first separate dictionary configuration mismatch from logged timestamp-spacing mismatch and investigate the responsible path.
caveats: No WCET, scheduling, deadline, overrun, processor-load, or real-time execution claim is supported.
Desktop-MIL timestamps do not establish target timing performance.

talkTrack: Keep roles explicit: initialization is the baseline producer, the driver is stimulus producer and executor, the harness is connectivity, the driver oracle computes pass fields, and validate_training_project is a later package validator that reads the retained CSV and checks file presence.
do: Trace one requirement from input row through harness output, oracle fields, exports, and package-validation summary.
expected: The learner can name who produced, executed, assessed, exported, and later checked the artifact set.
recovery: If provenance is unclear, do not merge files from different runs; retain timestamps and rerun the controlled producer chain only with authorization.
caveats: The limited suite retains 19 passing sample assessments from one deterministic 0.36-second desktop-MIL simulation.
The validator does not independently rerun the suite or establish export freshness.

talkTrack: State the result precisely: one 0.36-second desktop-MIL execution was assessed at nineteen rows/instants spaced at 0.02 seconds. All rows retain true NumericPass, LimiterActivePass, TimestampPass, and Timing50HzPass; the first three are row-specific and the suite-level spacing result is repeated on each row.
do: Open the CSV and identify boundary, saturation, invalid-input, disabled-mode, and mode-transition rows.
expected: The learner can explain why the dashboard says 19/19 and what each pass field represents.
recovery: If the badge and row data disagree, trust neither until the controlled driver is rerun and all exports are regenerated together.
caveats: This is not nineteen independent tests and not a Test Manager suite.
The report graphic supports review; CSV/MAT values and executable oracle determine retained status.

talkTrack: Read the test report top to bottom. The input display is clipped to plus or minus 18 for readability; expected and actual outputs overlap, valid Normal-mode commands clamp at plus or minus 12, and invalid or disabled rows use zero fallback. Expected and actual limiter_active overlap. The log-scale error panel is visually empty because every retained absolute error is exactly zero.
do: Select one row from each behavior class and match it across the top, middle, and error panels and the CSV.
expected: The learner explains all three panels, including why a blank log-error trace represents zero positive errors rather than missing data.
recovery: Use the CSV or MAT file for exact values when plot clipping, overlap, or log scaling hides detail.
caveats: Displayed input clipping does not change the executed input values.
The active flag is true only for valid Normal-mode input strictly outside the inclusive limits.
Use 'retains evidence of passing checks,' not 'proves certification compliance.'

talkTrack: Trace requirements to implementation and specific acceptance evidence. PRL-001 is associated with rows 1-10 and 19; PRL-004 covers 0.02-second configuration and logged spacing within the executable tolerance. PRL-005 covers same-frame magnitude response at row 10, not an unrelated invalid-input row.
do: Open docs/PitchRateLimiter_Requirements_Traceability.csv and trace one ID to a model artifact, a result column, and a representative retained row.
expected: The learner produces a defensible requirement-to-model-to-check-to-result chain and notices the corrected PRL-005 mapping.
recovery: If an ID cannot be tied to an observable criterion and row, mark the trace incomplete and correct the traceability record under change control.
caveats: The IDs are training records in CSV, not live Requirements Toolbox links.
Traceability supports review; it does not replace independent verification or approval.

talkTrack: FCS_Data.sldd is the shared Design Data source. It retains 31 entries: 26 Simulink.Parameter objects, four Simulink.Signal objects, and one Simulink.Bus. FlightControlBus has five scalar elements: q_rate, pitch_angle, mach, air_data_valid, and mode.
do: Compare Sample_time, q_limit_normal, q_fallback_command, and FlightControlBus between the dictionary and retained inventory CSV files.
expected: The learner locates the values, types, units, dimensions, descriptions, and five bus elements.
recovery: If inventories and dictionary disagree, treat the inventories as stale and regenerate them only through the controlled initialization/refresh workflow.
caveats: The dictionary and bus define controlled structure; they do not by themselves prove semantic correctness.
Values are illustrative classroom data.

talkTrack: The GUI and MATLAB API expose the same controlled entry. In Model Explorer open data/FCS_Data.sldd, select Design Data and FlightControlBus, or use Simulink.data.dictionary.open, getSection, getEntry, and getValue, then close the dictionary.
do: Run the exact API example on the slide and compare the returned element names with the Model Explorer capture and inventory CSV.
expected: The command returns q_rate, pitch_angle, mach, air_data_valid, and mode, and the dictionary closes cleanly.
recovery: If the entry is unresolved, confirm projectRoot and initialization; do not create a duplicate FlightControlBus in the base workspace.
caveats: Initialization can restore managed names; make edits only under the project's data-change process.
The screenshot was captured for read-only orientation.

talkTrack: Review contracts before aesthetics: exact learner model/harness names, saved Normal reference mode, controlled dictionary, fixed-step/sample-time agreement, explicit input provenance, no unexpected update diagnostic, practice-driver oracle ownership, learner-local evidence paths, traceability, and stated boundaries. The exact known Student-license Model-block message is documented separately from unexpected warnings.
do: Have a second person walk the checklist against the repository without relying on the presenter's memory.
expected: Each checklist item has a file, model property, command output, or explicitly Open disposition.
recovery: For any unsupported item, record the gap and owner; do not mark it complete based only on the deck.
caveats: A training peer review is not automatically the independent verification or approval required by a program.

prerequisite: Target component and project check configuration identified.
talkTrack: Use Model Advisor only after the program supplies the component, profile/check IDs, owner, and report path shown as TBD. Then launch Model Advisor, select the approved checks, run them, triage findings, correct or justify them, rerun, and retain the report with model/configuration identity and reviewer disposition.
do: Demonstrate how to open Model Advisor and locate check selection and report controls; label the activity FUTURE unless an approved profile is supplied and executed.
expected: The learner can explain how a component would be checked and how findings would be verified and retained.
recovery: If no approved check profile, report location, or disposition authority is known, stop at the walkthrough and record the gate Open.
caveats: No completed Model Advisor run, approved profile, retained report, or disposition record is supplied in this package.
A passing Advisor run would be one evidence input, not certification approval.

talkTrack: Reserve distinct controlled locations for Polyspace Bug Finder and Code Prover results. Record tool/version, configuration, source or generated-code baseline, findings, dispositions, reviewer, and rerun status when the approved process requires them.
do: Identify the project owner and approved storage location for each future artifact; do not paste an untraceable screenshot into the placeholder.
expected: Both placeholders remain visibly Open until traceable reports and dispositions are supplied.
recovery: If Polyspace is unavailable or not required, document the authoritative applicability decision instead of implying completion.
caveats: No Bug Finder or Code Prover execution or retained result is supplied.
Tool availability in an inventory does not mean analysis was run.

talkTrack: Place the training workflow in context: DO-178C addresses airborne software life-cycle objectives and DO-331 supplies model-based development and verification guidance. Project plans determine applicable objectives, tools, independence, records, and acceptance.
do: Map one training artifact to a plausible life-cycle data category, then identify what approved project plan would be needed to accept it.
expected: The learner can discuss relevance without claiming that the package is compliant or certifiable.
recovery: For program-specific interpretations, defer to the approved plans, certification authority, and designated engineering/quality roles.
caveats: This deck is educational and not a compliance finding, certification basis, or substitute for approved plans.

talkTrack: Software level and independence affect the rigor and separation of verification activities, but they are assigned by the program's safety and certification process. The model author should know who may independently verify and who may approve each record.
do: Identify the program-defined software level, required independence, verifier, and approver for the learner's actual project; leave blanks for this training package.
expected: The learner distinguishes author, reviewer/independent verifier when required, and approving authority.
recovery: If roles or level are unknown, treat sign-off as Open and escalate to engineering assurance or certification leadership.
caveats: No software level or program-specific independence determination is assigned by this training package.

talkTrack: Use bidirectional traceability across allocated requirement, model implementation, verification method, acceptance criterion, execution evidence, result, review, and disposition. The training CSV demonstrates a small local chain; a production process needs the approved system of record.
do: Trace PRL-004 forward to its checks and backward from a retained pass row to its requirement ID.
expected: The learner can identify missing links, not just follow a one-way hyperlink.
recovery: Record any orphan requirement, model behavior, or evidence artifact and assign an owner before baseline closure.
caveats: A CSV trace matrix is instructional here; it is not automatically an approved requirements-management baseline.

talkTrack: The PRL identifiers displayed in the deck and CSV are presentation/training IDs. They provide readable trace examples but are not live Requirements Toolbox objects or links to an approved external requirement baseline.
do: Locate where each displayed ID is defined and where it appears in retained result rows.
expected: The learner labels the IDs accurately and does not imply live requirement-link status.
recovery: If a project requires live links, create them only in the approved requirements repository and retain link-verification evidence.
caveats: No Requirements Toolbox link set or approved requirements database is supplied.

talkTrack: A CI lane would establish the environment, restore controlled data, update models, run authorized tests, build selected targets, validate artifacts, archive logs, and publish status with traceable provenance. This package supplies local scripts but no executed Jenkins pipeline.
do: Map each local script to a possible CI stage and identify required credentials, licenses, artifact retention, and failure gates.
expected: The learner produces a conceptual pipeline without claiming that automation has run.
recovery: If CI evidence is required, implement and execute it under the project's infrastructure and configuration-management process.
caveats: Jenkins executed: NO.
A conceptual CI diagram is not an executed pipeline or qualification record.

talkTrack: Classify before fixing: environment/path, controlled data, model update/interface, simulation/input, oracle/acceptance, export/provenance, build, or assurance/sign-off. The earliest failing gate usually provides the clearest diagnostic.
do: For a sample failure, record the command, target, first diagnostic, affected artifact, and category before changing anything.
expected: The learner proposes a scoped recovery that preserves evidence and avoids destructive regeneration.
recovery: Return to the last passing gate, correct one root cause, rerun only the dependent controlled stages, and retain diagnostics and dispositions.
caveats: Do not reclassify an unperformed assurance gate as a technical pass/fail.
Do not overwrite retained evidence while investigating an unexplained discrepancy.

talkTrack: Keep the PIL badge explicit: NOT PERFORMED. A successful desktop GRT build produces code and an executable; it does not execute that code in SIL or PIL or compare code behavior with the model.
do: Point to Executable executed: NO, Code-generation validation run: NO, and SIL/PIL run: NO in the build manifest.
expected: The learner can explain why 5/5 build success does not change PIL status.
recovery: If PIL is required, obtain the target, harness, comparison criteria, tools, and approved procedure, then retain a separate execution record.
caveats: No SIL, PIL, HIL, bench, or target execution evidence is supplied.

talkTrack: Read validator status with scope and freshness. It updates eight delivered models and requires every saved Model-reference mode to be Normal. On the Student license it accepts only the exact known Model-block fallback message for the two parent models; any other warning fails. It reads the retained limiter CSV and checks 24 named paths, but does not rerun the suite or establish freshness/hashes.
do: Open scripts/validate_training_project.m beside the summary and connect each reported count to the code that produces it.
expected: The learner states 8/8, 19/19, and 24/24 accurately and includes each limitation.
recovery: If current evidence is needed, rerun the controlled producers first, then the validator; preserve the old evidence set according to project rules.
caveats: Overall PASS is limited to the checks implemented by this validator.
Required-file presence is not proof of content correctness, freshness, or common provenance.
HIL executed: NO; Jenkins executed: NO.

talkTrack: Summarize what is retained versus explained versus future. Retained: saved models/data, update status, desktop-MIL runs, limiter oracle outputs, SDI artifacts, inventories, and one desktop GRT build. Explained: settings, logging/test-point choices, Advisor workflow, CI concept, and assurance context. Future: executed Advisor/Polyspace, SIL/PIL/HIL, production-code approval, and signed project records.
do: For every claimed result, name the exact file. For every future gate, name the required owner or authoritative process.
expected: No slide placeholder or instructional workflow is mistaken for completed evidence.
recovery: Remove or qualify any claim that lacks a retained artifact or authoritative disposition.
caveats: Desktop-MIL and GRT training evidence do not establish production-aircraft suitability or certification compliance.

prerequisite: Program-defined completion form, roles, and authority identified.
talkTrack: Treat RCF as the user's project-defined completion-record placeholder, not a universal acronym or authority. The visible form/path, process owner, and trigger remain TBD until the approved process supplies them. Only then should the record identify model/version/requirements/evidence/configuration/findings and required signatures/dates.
do: Locate the approved program form and storage location; identify owner, trigger, required signers, and the evidence package it references.
expected: The slide remains an Open placeholder until the approved record is completed and signed after model and verification closure.
recovery: If the form, meaning, or authority is unknown, do not invent one; escalate to the project's quality/certification owner and keep the gate Open.
caveats: No RCF, signature, independent-verification record, or approval record is supplied in this training package.
Passing MIL, Model Advisor, or Polyspace checks would be evidence inputs, not substitutes for required review and acceptance.

prerequisite: Core slides 1-46 reviewed; write permission only where authorized.
talkTrack: Demonstrate the learner-owned chain end to end: preflight, unique tag, safe practice component + matching harness creation, Ctrl+D, practice-driver execution, learner-local 19/19 interpretation, SDI causal reading, dictionary access, one requirement trace, and open-gate declaration. Reproducing the delivered baseline is a separate action.
do: Create learner_workspace/<tag>, run its practice assessment, and record exact model/harness/output paths, one SDI transient explanation, all three result-panel explanations, one requirement trace, and remaining assurance gates.
expected: A reviewer repeats the learner creation and assessment path without retargeting the delivered harness or overwriting controlled baseline results.
recovery: Stop at the first failed gate, classify it using slide 42, preserve diagnostics, and resume only after the prerequisite is restored.
caveats: Do not rebuild or refresh evidence merely to obtain a green screen when authorization or provenance is unclear.
The retained build manifest records Git dirty at build = 1; disclose that provenance when citing it.

talkTrack: Close on repeatable engineering behavior: know the target, initialize explicitly, update before execution, use controlled inputs and oracles, interpret plots causally, retain provenance, trace requirements, and leave unperformed assurance gates visibly Open.
do: State one retained result, one evidence limitation, one recovery rule, and one next owner/action.
expected: The learner can hand off the package without overclaiming scope or completion.
recovery: If any claim cannot be tied to a source, revise the handoff before sign-off.
caveats: End state is onboarding readiness, not certification, production-code approval, or signed program acceptance.

talkTrack: Use the glossary to align MATLAB, Simulink, MIL, SDI, GRT, SIL, PIL, HIL, WCET, and traceability terms with the boundaries used in this deck.
do: Look up any term before using it in an evidence claim.
expected: Terminology remains consistent across the learner's handoff.
recovery: If a program defines a term differently, cite the approved project definition.
caveats: A glossary aids communication and does not assign certification status.

talkTrack: Use the aircraft loop and subsystem gallery to understand command, tracking error, controller, saturation, actuator dynamics, plant, sensor lag, disturbance, and feedback as an illustrative closed-loop architecture.
do: Trace pitch command to measured feedback and open each referenced subsystem view shown in the gallery.
expected: The learner names the causal path and the signals used by the SDI explanation.
recovery: If a subsystem view differs, inspect the saved model rather than relying only on the exported image.
caveats: The plant and controller are simplified training models, not identified or certifiable aircraft models.

talkTrack: The Stateflow training model illustrates OFF, ARMED, ENGAGED, and DEGRADED behavior and the relationship between chart-level state logic and root-level Simulink interfaces.
do: Trace an arm, engage, invalid-data degradation, and reset sequence in the chart and retained mode-sequence output.
expected: The learner identifies visited modes and the control-enabled condition.
recovery: If Stateflow is unavailable, inspect the exported chart image and retained CSV; do not claim interactive execution.
caveats: The mode logic is illustrative and not a production autopilot state machine.

talkTrack: Use the highest-level architecture to see bus input, sensor processing, mode interpretation, pitch-rate limiting, controller, actuator command, and referenced-model boundaries. This is also the v8 GRT build target.
do: Trace the four Model blocks and confirm each saved SimulationMode is Normal.
expected: The learner identifies SensorProcessingRef, PitchRateLimiter, PitchControllerRef, and ActuatorCommandRef and relates them to the 5/5 build.
recovery: If a reference is unresolved or not Normal, restore the models path and saved baseline before updating or building.
caveats: Successful reference resolution and compilation do not establish component verification or production readiness.

talkTrack: The component gallery provides reviewable contracts for sensor processing, limiter, controller, and actuator command. Use names, types, units, sample time, parameters, and fallback behavior to reason across reference boundaries.
do: Select one component and compare its root ports, dictionary entries, and use in the top architecture.
expected: The learner can state the component's inputs, outputs, responsibility, and controlled parameters.
recovery: If the contract is unclear, return to the saved model, dictionary inventory, and bus inventory rather than inferring from layout.
caveats: The gallery is an orientation aid; the saved model and controlled data are authoritative within this training package.

talkTrack: Use overlays to connect visual annotation with the underlying model and results. Labels should identify navigation, signal purpose, or evidence relationship without obscuring the original artifact.
do: Choose one overlay and verify every callout against the saved model or retained result file.
expected: The learner distinguishes editorial guidance from model-generated annotations and evidence.
recovery: If a callout disagrees with the source artifact, correct the overlay and retain the source unchanged.
caveats: Editorial overlays are explanatory and are not independent verification evidence.

talkTrack: Keep callback and verification paths separate. The callback example creates and loads deterministic context for standalone exploration; run_pitch_rate_limiter_tests initializes the baseline, injects the nineteen-point harness inputs, simulates, applies the oracle, and writes retained evidence.
do: Trace preload, setup, postload, optional standalone simulation, and cleanup, then compare that lane with the harness driver.
expected: The learner identifies which path creates context and which path owns the retained assessment oracle and reports.
recovery: If callback state persists, run the project cleanup workflow and verify the base/model workspace before executing the harness driver.
caveats: callback_workflow_example.m does not invoke the retained harness test driver.
Callbacks create context; they do not by themselves create verification evidence.
